description: Iterate lazily through a string encoded as repeated character/count pairs. Example 1: the encoding A2B1 yields A, A, B, then a space after exhaustion. Example 2: a run count of zero contributes no output, and an exhausted iterator still returns a space. Constraints: characters are letters, counts are nonnegative decimal integers, and the encoding is valid.
intuition: Only the current run and its remaining count are needed to produce the next character.

brute_force.approach: Expand every run into a complete string before serving iterator calls.

optimal.approach: Parse run pairs once and advance through them only when the current count is exhausted.
optimal.time: construction O(encoded length), next O(1) amortized, hasNext O(1)

edge_cases: A run count may contain multiple digits.
next returns a single space when no characters remain.
